Naturalistic 16:9 coastal commercial still, modern social-first beauty lifestyle photography with tactile editorial energy and true-to-life color, shot like a sun-soaked campaign frame you would screenshot. SCARLETT (Image 1) in a black long-sleeve rash vest worn as a swim top, half-peeled and damp against her, simple flip-flops on the concrete, salt-stiff hair and sandy calves, mid-motion at the parked sedan as a sun-faded canvas tote slams onto the warm white bonnet and she upends it, sunscreen and a cracked hair claw spilling across the metal while a slim tube of the product from (CORAL_LIPSTICK (Image 3)) tumbles in the air and her hand snaps toward it, fingers spread, body coiled with potential energy, mid-breath, gaze locked on the falling tube rather than the camera. Open Bondi Beach car park in early morning: pale sun-warmed poured concrete bays stretching away, utilitarian metal safety rail, empty-ish spaces, everyday beach clutter, chrome trim and white paint flashing, the ocean a hard bright horizontal strip of blue beyond the rail, heat already lifting off the deck. Hard unfiltered early-morning sun raking the white bonnet and chrome, clean directional shadows, bright coastal bounce filling the shadows, high-key airy light with crisp whites and one coral accent catching enamel flash. Slightly above eye-level handheld lifestyle angle, shallow depth of field holding the tumbling tube and reaching hand sharp against a soft ocean-strip bokeh, anamorphic coastal flares, clean bright grade with warm highlights and lifted shadows.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
